Details.JobSummary: This position is part of the Department of War, Defense Security Cooperation Agency. This is a Tier III SES level position.
Details.AgencyMarketingStatement: DSCA's mission is to advance U.S. national security and foreign policy interests by building the capacity of foreign security forces to respond to shared challenges. DSCA leads the broader U.S. security cooperation enterprise in its efforts to train, educate, advise, and equip foreign partners. DSCA administers security cooperation programs that support U.S. policy interests and objectives.
MajorDuties: This position is part of the Department of War, Defense Security Cooperation Agency (DSCA). DSCA is responsible for planning, coordinating, administering, and supervising Department of War (DOW) programs for transfer of defense articles, services, and technology, by sale or grant to foreign governments and international organizations. These programs include Foreign Military Sales (FMS) under which defense articles and services are sold to foreign countries or international organizations, Foreign Military Financing (FMF) under which grants or loans are provided to foreign countries for financing of FMS or direct commercial contracts with U.S. industry, International Military Education and Training (IMET) under which financial assistance is provided to foreign students attending U.S. military schools, and Humanitarian Assistance and Demining (HAID) and Overseas Humanitarian Disaster and Civic Aid (OHDACA), as well as other Title 10 security cooperation authorities (section 332 and 333 authorities), under which support is provided to foreign governments.. DUTIES: In accordance with US Code, Title 10, Section 382, is responsible for the execution and administration of all security cooperation programs and activities of the DoW involving the provision of defense articles, military training, and other defense-related services by grant, loan, cash sale, or lease. Directs, administers, and provides DoW-wide security cooperation administration and execution guidance. Plans, manages, and directs DSCA, its subordinate elements, and all assigned resources, including by setting organization goals and priorities, allocating organizational resources, and managing internal relationships. Oversees and exercises overall management responsibility for the Defense Security Cooperation University (DSCU), which provides consolidated Security Cooperation training and education for the Security Cooperation Workforce and the broader Security Cooperation enterprise. Represents the interests of the Secretary of War and the Under Secretary of War for Acquisition and Sustainment (USW(A&S)) in security cooperation matters. Manages the Defense Security Cooperation Service (DSCS), which manages the manning, training, and administrative support for military and civilian Security Cooperation Offices around the world.

Details.JobSummary: This position is part of the Department of War, Defense Security Cooperation Agency (DSCA). This is a Tier II SES level position.
Details.AgencyMarketingStatement: Our Mission DSCA's mission is to advance U.S. national security and foreign partners in order to encourage and enable allies and partners to respond to shared challenges. DSCA leads the broader U.S. security cooperation enterprise in its efforts to train, educate, advise, and equip foreign partners. Our Vision DSCA's vision is to lead the Security Cooperation enterprise in delivering effective, enduring, and timely solutions, and serve as the source for SC expertise and innovation for our defense and foreign policy stakeholders to ensure the United States remains the global partner of choice. Our Values DSCA incorporates our values into every aspect of performing our mission and planning for the future. These values are: Proactive, Accountable, Respectful, Transparent, Networked, Empowered, Representative.
MajorDuties: Serves as the senior executive responsible for the administration, accountability, audit readiness, and financial stewardship of the Department's multi-billion-dollar Security Assistance Accounts (SAA) authorized under Title 22, ensuring compliance with statutory, regulatory, and Departmental requirements. Orchestrates the budget formulation process for DSCA's unique multi-year substantivefinancial programs, encompassing analysis, planning, scheduling, and coordination of all phases of the Agency's budgeting process to determine resource allocation, sequence, and timing of actions funded through unique non-appropriated and appropriated funds sources. Governs the long-range forecasting, day-to-day administration, and solvency of the Department's FMS Trust Fund, working directly with the Defense Financial Accounting Service (DFAS). Exercises executive authority over the allocation of the multi-billion-dollar FMS and FMF administrative funds to U.S. Implementing Agencies (IAs), geographic Combatant Commands (CCMDs), War Agencies, and DFAS. Directs the annual Security Assistance Program and Budget Review (SAPBR) process, collaborating with the DSCA Director, Military Department leaders, and other senior officials to finalize the fiscal year (FY) FMS budgets for all Military Departments and implementing agencies. Commands all aspects of the PPBE processes and advises the DSCA Director on budgeting and fiscal planning activities. Provides executive oversight of the development and publication of resource management decisions (RMD) applicable to the enterprise-wide security cooperation community. Drives strategic engagement with a broad spectrum of internal and external executive stakeholders to plan, operate, and provide overall financial oversight for the DoW's multi-billion-dollar FMS, FMF, and building partner capacity (BPC) programs. Architects the SAA's financial strategy and policy, providing recurrent updates and authoritative technical guidance for the SAA to the Department's Deputy Comptroller and Deputy CFO to ensure alignment with the long-range plans of the Department's Title 10 financial operations. Executes the Department's FMF programs. Spearheads the analysis, execution, and assessment techniques for diverse lending tools, encompassing federally guaranteed loans for our nation's foreign partners to achieve their defense needs; oversees the drafting of legislative proposals for novel, government-backed loan solutions to bolster the Defense Industrial Base (DIB) and partner needs. Implements programs for rigorous fiscal oversight of security cooperation funds, with the authority to rescind or withhold funding for major programs and decide the stipulations for utilizing these funds, in consultation with the DSCA Director. Drives financial responsibility and technological innovation by reviewing and approving international agreements and administering the security cooperation credit management system. Directs DSCA's contracting and acquisition support program services, providing executive oversight over DSCA's overall acquisition support process, involving major DSCA programs and initiatives.

MatchedObjectDescriptor.QualificationSummary: Eligibility will be based upon a clear showing the applicant has education, training, and experience of the scope and quality sufficient to effectively carry-out the duties of the position. Candidates must exemplify the corporate perspective, leadership vision, broad experience and character needed in the SES corps not only to satisfy the immediate vacancy, but future vacancies which will occur in a variety of organizations, functions and locations. Candidates will not be hired based on their race, sex, color, religion, or national origin. In accordance with new OPM requirements to streamline Senior Executive Service (SES) hiring, applicants are no longer required to submit lengthy narrative essays, including those for Executive Core Qualifications (ECQs) or Mandatory Technical Qualifications (TQs), when applying. Instead, the initial application will be resume-only, capped at two pages. This change streamlines the application process and more closely aligns with private industry practices. Applicants identified for potential selection will have their ECQs assessed by undergoing a structured interview with the Office of Personnel Management (OPM) Qualifications Review Board (QRB). To meet the minimum qualification requirements for this position, you must show that you possess the education, Technical Qualifications (TQ), and Executive Core Qualifications (ECQ) related to this position within your resume (not to exceed 2 pages). Resumes over the 2-page limit will be disqualified. Your resume should include examples of experience, education, and accomplishments applicable to the qualification(s). If your resume does not reflect demonstrated evidence of the ECQs and TQs, you may not receive further consideration for the position. CERTIFICATIONS: DAWIA PM Practitioner or PM Level II Legacy TECHNICAL QUALIFICATIONS (TQs): Your resume should demonstrate accomplishments that satisfy the technical qualifications. TQ1: (Critical) Executive level acquisition experience, with special emphasis on fielding proliferated systems on rapid acquisition timelines. TQ2: Proven expertise executing the entire Planning, Programming, Budgeting, and Execution (PPBE) process with program inputs and equities at the Service, Department, Secretariat, and Interagency levels. TQ3: Demonstrated successfully field applied technology programs at the 6.4 (advanced component development and prototyping), 6.5 (systems development and demonstration), and 6.7 (operational system development) levels. EXECUTIVE CORE QUALIFICATIONS (ECQs): All new appointees to the Senior Executive Service (SES) under a career appointment will be assessed for executive competency against the five mandatory ECQs: ECQ 1. Commitment to the Rule of Law and the Principles of the American Founding: Demonstrated knowledge of the American system of government, commitment to uphold the Constitution and the rule of law, and commitment to serve the American people. ECQ 2. Driving Efficiency: Demonstrated ability to strategically and efficiently manage resources, budget effectively, cut wasteful spending, and pursue efficiency through process and technological upgrades. ECQ 3. Merit and Competence: Demonstrated knowledge, ability, and technical competence to effectively and reliably produce work that is of exceptional quality. ECQ 4. Leading People: Demonstrated ability to lead and inspire a group toward meeting the organization's vision, mission, and goals, and to drive a high-performance, high-accountability culture. This includes, when necessary, the ability to lead people through change and to hold individuals accountable. ECQ 5. Achieving Results: Demonstrated ability to achieve both individual and organizational results, and to align results to stated goals from superiors. Please note: If you are a member of the SES or have been certified through successful participation in an OPM approved SES Candidate Development Program, or have SES reinstatement eligibility, you must attach proof (e.g., SF-50 or Certification by OPM's SES Qualifications Review Board) of your eligibility for noncompetitive appointment to the SES.

To achieve that mission, the Air Force has a vision of Global Vigilance, Reach and Power. That vision orbits around three core competencies: Developing Airmen, Technology-to-Warfighting and Integrating Operations. Core competencies and distinctive capabilities are based on a shared commitment to three core values -- integrity first, service before self, and excellence in all we do.

Candidates will not be hired based on their race, sex, color, religion, or national origin. To meet the minimum qualification requirements for this position, you must show that you possess the Executive Core Qualifications (ECQ) and Mandatory Technical Qualifications (MTQ) related to this position within your resume. Your Resume must be 2 pages. If you submit a resume that exceeds the two-page limit, you will immediately be deemed ineligible for this position and will receive no further consideration. We recommend using a sans-serif font such as Lato, if available. Other acceptable options include Calibri, Helvetica, Arial, Verdana, Open Sans, Source Sans Pro, Roboto, or Noto Sans. Please use 0.5-inch margins. For formatting, consider using a 14-point font for titles and a 10-point font for the main body text. Your resume should include examples of experience, education, and accomplishments applicable to the qualification(s). If your resume does not reflect demonstrated evidence of these qualifications, you may not receive consideration for the position. There is NO requirement to prepare a separate narrative statement specifically addressing the Executive Core Qualifications (ECQs) or the Mandatory Technical Qualification (MTQ). MANDATORY TECHNICAL QUALIFICATION (MTQ): Your resume should demonstrate accomplishments that would satisfy the following mandatory technical qualification. MTQ: Demonstrated ability to manage and technically lead a large, diverse research and technology organization across the sciences of biological and biotechnology, electromagnetic spectrum, energy, information, humans in complex systems, mechanical, network, cyber, and computational, photonics, electronics and quantum, extreme materials, terminal effects, and weapons, supported by a distinguished record of research quality, publications, and professional recognition, alongside proven experience advocating for and defending program recommendations in adversarial technical and managerial environments. EXECUTIVE CORE QUALIFICATIONS (ECQs): In addition to the Mandatory Technical Qualification Requirements listed above, all new entrants into the Senior Executive Service (SES) under a career appointment will be assessed for executive competency against the following five mandatory ECQs. If your 2-page resume does not reflect demonstrated evidence of the ECQs and MTQ, you may not receive further consideration for the position. There are five ECQs: ECQ 1: Commitment to the Rule of Law and the Principles of the American Founding - This core qualification requires a demonstrated knowledge of the American system of government, commitment to uphold the Constitution and the rule of law, and commitment to serve the American people. ECQ 2: Driving Efficiency - This core qualification involves the demonstrated ability to strategically and efficiently manage resources, budget effectively, cut wasteful spending, and pursue efficiency through process and technological upgrades. ECQ 3: Merit and Competence - This core qualification involves the demonstrated knowledge, ability and technical competence to effectively and reliably produce work that is of exceptional quality. ECQ 4: Leading People - This core qualification involves the demonstrated ability to lead and inspire a group toward meeting the organization's vision, mission, and goals, and to drive a high-performance, high-accountability culture. This includes, when necessary, the ability to lead people through change and to hold individuals accountable. ECQ 5: Achieving Results - This core qualification involves the demonstrated ability to achieve both individual and organizational results, and to align results to stated goals from superiors. Note: If you are a member of the SES or have been certified through successful participation in an OPM approved SES Candidate Development Program (SESCDP), or have SES reinstatement eligibility, you do not need to respond to the ECQs. Instead, you should attach proof (e.g., SF-50, Certification by OPM's SES Qualifications Review Board (QRB)) of your eligibility for noncompetitive appointment to the SES.

Details.AgencyMarketingStatement: Civilian employees serve a vital role in supporting the Army mission. They provide the skills that are not readily available in the military, but crucial to support military operations. The Army integrates the talents and skills of its military and civilian members to form a Total Army. This position is in the Senior Executive Service (SES) which is a small elite group of top government leaders. SES members possess a diverse portfolio of experiences including strong skills to lead across organizations. MajorDuties: The Extramural Research Office (ERO) serves under the supervision of the Futures and Autonomous Systems Command (FASCOM), Combat Capabilities Development Command (DEVCOM), Army Research Laboratory (ARL) Director. The DEVCOM ARL is responsible for providing guidance in terms of broadly defined Army, T2COM, DEVCOM & ARL policies, mission and functions. To include a workforce of approximately 91 civilians professional, scientific, administrative, technical, and support personnel including 2 STs and 4 DB-Vs; 1 military; and approximately 21 contract personnel. Civilian S&T workforce consists of DB-02/03/04 (GS07-15 equivalent), primarily at the DB-03 level. Serves as the Director, Extramural Research Office. Responsible for setting and executing the nationwide extramural research agenda and programs on Army focused basic research within the biological and biotechnology; electromagnetic spectrum; energy; information; humans in complex systems; mechanical; network, cyber, & computational; photonics, electronics & quantum; extreme materials; terminal effects; and weapons sciences to provide critical enhancements to current warfighter needs and revolutionary advances required for technological dominance of the future force with emphasis on the Army's Modernization Priorities. Manages an annual Army Research Office (ARO) budget exceeding $253M in order to provide full life cycle management from topic formulation through scientific and fiscal program execution. Manages technology transition initiation for more than 1,700 grants and contracts performed by approximately 3,500 researchers at approximately 300 universities and businesses. Responsible for oversight of the entire ARL extramural 6.1 program. Serves as a member of high-level executive scientific and technology committees and groups at the international, national, Office of the Secretary of War, Department of the Army, and other Federal Agency levels, providing technical expertise and influencing executive- level policy and programs. Exercises line authority and technical direction over the total office program. Acquisition Position Information: 1. This is a Critical Acquisition Position (CAP). Details.JobSummary: The Deputy Assistant Secretary of War for Health Readiness Policy and Oversight is the principal staff assistant and advisor to the Assistant Secretary of War for Health Affairs for all Department of War deployment medicine policies, programs, and activities.

SES members possess a diverse portfolio of experiences including strong skills to lead across organizations. As a Senior Executive, you will influence the direction of innovation and transformation of the federal government and lead the next generation of public servants. The Office of the Secretary of War (OSW) is the principal staff element of the Secretary of War in the exercise of policy development, planning, resource management, and program evaluation responsibilities. OSW includes the Offices of the Secretary and Deputy Secretary of War, Under Secretaries of War, Assistant Secretaries of War, General Counsel of the DoW; Director of Cost Assessment and Program Evaluation; Inspector General of the DoW; Director of Operational Test and Evaluation; Chief Information Officer of the DoW; Assistant to the Secretary of War for Public Affairs; Chief Digital and Artificial Intelligence Officer; and the Director of Administration and Management.
MajorDuties: The Deputy Assistant Secretary of War for Health Readiness Policy and Oversight is the senior advisor and agent of the Assistant Secretary of War for Health Affairs and in carrying out these responsibilities directs Department-wide efforts to engage in the policy cycle to develop and analyze policies and oversee implementation and execution of policies and programs relating to Department of War (DoW) force health protection and readiness for 2.2 million service members. Responsibilities encompass a broad range and variety of functions and activities that are vital in supporting the mission of the Military Health System. Major duties and responsibilities include, but are not limited to: Responsible for force health protection and readiness doctrine, and the elements of the policy cycle and oversight, to include agenda setting, formulation, adoption, implementation, and evaluation. Guides and directs the policy cycle for provision of care in support of readiness and contingency operations and oversees the programs that enable deployment of fully trained and equipped medical personnel and units. Provides policy and oversight of the Combat Support Agency functions of the Defense Health Agency. Provides policy and oversight of all DoW issuances assigned to Health Readiness Policy and Readiness. Develops policy, defends requirements, and advocates for the utilization and integration of new technologies to improve efficiency, effectiveness, and quality of the military health care system in the deployed or contingency environment. Provides policy guidance and oversight in the functional areas of medical logistics, medical materiel supply chain, pharmaceuticals, manpower and personnel, resource methodologies, and information systems. Oversees and develops policies, strategies, and plans that govern the management of the Defense Health Program medical research, development, and acquisition programs.

MatchedObjectDescriptor.QualificationSummary: Eligibility will be based upon a clear showing the applicant has training, education and experience of the scope and quality sufficient to effectively carry-out the duties of the position. Candidates must exemplify the corporate perspective, leadership vision, broad experience and character needed in the SES corps not only to satisfy the immediate vacancy, but future vacancies which will occur in a variety of organizations, functions and locations. In accordance with the new OPM requirements to streamline Senior Executive Service (SES) hiring, applicants are no longer required to submit lengthy narrative essays, including those for Executive Core Qualifications (ECQs) or Mandatory Technical Qualifications (TQs) when applying. Instead, the initial application will be resume-only, capped at two pages. This change streamlines the application process and more closely aligns with private industry practice. Applicants identified for potential selection will have their ECQs assessed by undergoing a structured interview with the Office of Personnel Management (OPM) Qualifications Review Board. To meet minimum qualifications requirements for this position, you must show that you possess the education, Technical Qualifications (TQ) and Executive Core Qualifications (ECQ) related to this position within your resume (not to exceed 2 pages). Resumes over the 2-page limit will be disqualified. Your resume should include examples of experience, education and accomplishments applicable to the qualification(s). If your resume does not reflect demonstrated evidence of the ECQs and TQs, you may not receive further consideration for this position. CERTIFICATION: This position will require DAWIA APDP Level III Certification in any acquisition profession career field and member of Acquisition Corps that must be obtained within 4 years of of encumbering this position. TQ1: Demonstrated ability to lead a large, globally dispersed, and functionally diverse services acquisition organization. The ideal candidate must describe their experience overseeing a complex portfolio of programs comparable in scope to AMIC's $22B portfolio, which supports worldwide operations. This includes experience managing the integration of multiple acquisition and support functions (e.g., Program Management, Contracting, Engineering, Logistics, Finance, and Legal) to deliver mission-critical capabilities. Candidates should provide specific examples of how they have allocated resources, managed personnel, and ensured effective execution to support the strategic objectives of a major command or agency. TQ2: Demonstrated ability to develop and implement a strategic vision to transform acquisition processes for enhanced speed, agility, and lethality. The ideal candidate must describe their experience in challenging the status quo by introducing innovative acquisition strategies, such as commercial solutions openings and outcome-based contracting, to meet urgent warfighter needs. This includes providing specific examples of leading organizational change, fostering a culture of innovation and informed risk-taking, and effectively engaging with senior leaders across the Department of War, other government agencies, and the industrial base to shape policy and align enterprise acquisition efforts with the National Defense Strategy. IDEAL CANDIDATE: The ideal candidate for the Director of ACC AMIC must be an elite, visionary acquisition executive possessing a minimum of 10 years of senior-level acquisition experience, including at least 4 years in a Critical Acquisition Position and a mandatory DAWIA Level III (or professional equivalent) certification in Contracting or Program Management. A candidate with strong Contracting background is preferred as the position requires significant depth in contracting rules, regulations (i.e., the new Revolutionary Federal Acquisition Regulations), and best practices to oversee the implementation and execution of innovative acquisition strategies, complex source selections and source selection teams, and post-award contract management. The best candidate will possess a proven track record of leading complex, multi-functional organizations, and a demonstrated mastery of managing multi-billion-dollar acquisition portfolios, specifically focusing on large-scale services acquisitions, program management, strategic sourcing, and global operational program execution. To succeed in this high-impact role the candidate must have a deep understanding of the entire acquisition lifecycle from requirements generation to contract execution. Furthermore, they must be an innovative and agile leader capable of securing critical resources and driving cultural and procedural transformation, alongside a history of directing and developing highly diverse, multi-disciplinary teams of military, civilian, and contractor personnel. Crucially, the candidate must possess the political acumen and strategic communication skills required to represent the command at the highest echelons of the Department of War, Headquarters Air Force, and the Defense Industrial Base. Ultimately, the selected leader will be a transformative agent change who champions innovative, agile acquisition pathways and outcome-based contracting strategies to rapidly deliver lethal capabilities directly to the joint warfighter. EXECUTIVE CORE QUALIFICATIONS (ECQs): All new appointees to the Senior Executive Service (SES) under a career appointment will be assessed for executive competency against the five mandatory ECQs: ECQ 1. Commitment to the Rule of Law and the Principles of the American Founding: Demonstrated knowledge of the American system of government, commitment to uphold the Constitution and the rule of law, and commitment to serve the American people. ECQ 2. Driving Efficiency: Demonstrated ability to strategically and efficiently manage resources, budget effectively, cut wasteful spending, and pursue efficiency through process and technological upgrades. ECQ 3. Merit and Competence: Demonstrated knowledge, ability, and technical competence to effectively and reliably produce work that is of exceptional quality. ECQ 4. Leading People: Demonstrated ability to lead and inspire a group toward meeting the organization's vision, mission, and goals, and to drive a high-performance, high-accountability culture. This includes, when necessary, the ability to lead people through change and to hold individuals accountable. ECQ 5. Achieving Results: Demonstrated ability to achieve both individual and organizational results, and to align results to stated goals from superiors. Please note: If you are a member of the SES or have been certified through successful participation in an OPM approved SES Candidate Development Program, or have SES reinstatement eligibility, you must attach proof (e.g., SF-50 or Certification by OPM's SES Qualifications Review Board) of your eligibility for noncompetitive appointment to the SES. In addition, DoD requires an Enterprise Perspective. The individual must possess a broad point of view and an awareness and understanding of individual or organizational responsibilities in relation to DoD or government-wide strategic priorities. Executives should demonstrate ability to work with internal and external partners to support national security objectives. This perspective is typically gained through a variety of diverse work experiences. A separate narrative statement is not required--this information should be embedded within the application package.

Details.AgencyMarketingStatement: The mission of the United States Air Force is to fly, fight and win...airpower anytime, anywhere. To achieve that mission, the Air Force has a vision of Global Vigilance, Reach and Power. That vision orbits around three core competencies: Developing Airmen, Technology-to-Warfighting and Integrating Operations. Core competencies and distinctive capabilities are based on a shared commitment to three core values -- integrity first, service before self, and excellence in all we do. MajorDuties: The Director of the Air Combat Command Acquisition Management and Integration Center (ACC AMIC) leads a highly complex, globally dispersed services acquisition enterprise with a multi-billion-dollar portfolio supporting critical, worldwide warfighting operations across three Combatant Commands. In this capacity, the Director is responsible for the strategic planning, policy formulation, and execution of a $22 billion acquisition portfolio, which includes high-visibility programs like MQ-9 operations, Contract Adversary Air Support (AdAir), and international counternarcotics initiatives spanning 210 countries. The incumbent secures vital financial, manpower, and material resources to maintain readiness across all detachments and operating locations. Additionally, the Director exercises direct managerial control over a diverse, multi-disciplinary team of 535 military, civilian, and contractor personnel, actively fostering their professional development. Finally, the Director serves as the primary Air Combat Command representative in high-level Secretary of the Air Force (SAF), Headquarters Air Force (HAF), and cross-MAJCOM forums, ensuring strategic alignment and advocate-level representation for the command's acquisition and sourcing requirements.

MatchedObjectDescriptor.QualificationSummary: Eligibility for this executive level position will be based upon a clear demonstration that the applicant has experience of the scope and quality sufficient to effectively carry out the assignments of the position. Successful applicants will be distinguished from other applicants by a review of the Executive Competencies, Technical Competencies, Technical Qualifications, Intelligence Community Senior Officer Core Qualifications, and Education Requirements, if required. An applicant's resume must show that their experience, education and accomplishments reflect the competence and professional standing required to provide expertise needed for this position. INTELLIGENCE COMMUNITY SENIOR OFFICER CORE QUALIFICATIONS (ICSOCQ) Leading the Intelligence Enterprise. This core qualification involves the ability to integrate resources, information, interests, and activities effectively in support of the Intelligence Community's (IC) mission and to lead and leverage cross-organizational collaborative networks to achieve significant mission results. Inherent to this senior officer qualification is a deep understanding of the Intelligence enterprise and a shared commitment to the IC's core values. TECHNICAL QUALIFICATIONS (TQs) TQ 1. Executive/expert level experience leading a large, complex operations or production unit., including programming, budgeting and resourcing. TQ 2. Demonstrated change management skills focused on introducing new technology to achieve greater mission outcomes. TQ 3. Broad understanding of international (e.g., International Hydrographic Organization), Inter-Agency, Inter-Governmental Organizations (IGO), Non-Governmental Organizations (NGO), multi-lateral and bi-lateral arrangements directly related or similar to those impacting maritime safety of navigation (SoN) processes. TQ 4. Broad understanding of the DoD and civil (e.g. National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration) maritime community and its associated organizations, policies and programs. TQ 5. Demonstrated knowledge of the technical requirements, capabilities and challenges related to mapping, charting and digital navigation. EDUCATION REQUIREMENT Bachelor's degree from an accredited college or university. DESIRABLE QUALIFICATION CRITERIA: In addition to the mandatory qualifications, experience in the following is desired: 1. Experience in a maritime related field (cartography, bathymetry, maritime analysis, maritime navigation) 2. Knowledge of current and future DoD maritime navigation requirements. 3. Expert level knowledge regarding production of maritime related products and data.

MajorDuties: The Deputy Director, Maritime Safety Office (DD/SFH) is accountable for the development, sustainment, accuracy, and currency of a global maritime Safety of Navigation (SoN) product portfolio used to support navigation aboard all Department of War (DoW) surface and subsurface naval vessels. The DD/SFH develops and executes strategy to achieve long-term mission outcomes within the constraints of U.S. Code, international treaties, and applicable standards, and ensures alignment with NGA strategic objectives and mission imperatives. The DD/SFH maintains a deep understanding of the producer-mariner relationship and advances effective user engagement by interfacing with senior military leaders across the Services, FVEY and other international partners, and key multinational organizations including the International Hydrographic Organization (IHO) and NATO. The DD/SFH supports global readiness by assessing user needs; evaluating product availability, production timelines, and distribution pathways; and recommending strategies to optimize dissemination and operational utility. The DD/SFH works across the DoW, Intelligence Community (IC), and international partnerships to drive modernization of maritime SoN capabilities, with emphasis on implementing the S-100 Universal Hydrographic Framework. The DD/SFH leads and coordinates modernization initiatives that introduce new data sources, technologies, and production processes to improve quality, increase throughput, and strengthen resiliency of SoN production. The DD/SFH engages senior intelligence, defense, national, and international stakeholders on matters of national and international interest to share data, information, and tradecraft; establish collaborative practices; and shape doctrine, operating concepts, and business models impacting the GEOINT enterprise across the IC and DoW. The DD/SFH represents the IC and DoW in national and international forums to advance data sharing, cost/burden sharing, and cooperative production arrangements supporting next-generation Foundation GEOINT services. The DD/SFH oversees the quality, accuracy, and timeliness of geospatial information produced in-house, via contractors, and through national and international co-producers in support of military, civil, and allied partners. The DD/SFH provides leadership and oversight for SFH strategic integration and modernization, and maintains broad knowledge of maritime products and data, including the systems and workflows supporting in-house production, co-production, commodity sourcing, and contract-based data extraction, analysis, and finishing. As a member of the Source executive leadership team, the DD/SFH contributes to enterprise modernization efforts aligned to agency, component, and group-level Strategic Objectives, including data sharing and integration, collection, workforce development, and dissemination across the Source enterprise, supporting a modern, outcome-driven organization. The DD/SFH translates organizational priorities into executable programs and is accountable for office performance through direct management and oversight of division chiefs and senior staff. The incumbent leads a workforce of approximately 400 personnel (federal civilian, military, and contractor) located across NGA-Washington, NGA-St. Louis, the National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration (NOAA), and overseas locations. The DD/SFH plans, defends, and executes a multi-million-dollar annual budget through the Planning, Programming, Budgeting, and Execution (PPBE) process; adjusts objectives, work plans, schedules, and resource allocations as needed; and exercises sound judgment in managing Source enterprise-level contracts supporting maritime SoN requirements. The DD/SFH supports the Director, SFH in representing the Director, Source Operations and Management Directorate as the SoN mission manager, and the Director, NGA in the SoN functional management role. The DD/SFH partners closely with the SoN Senior GEOINT Advisor (SGA) and the Maritime SGA to execute and oversee the maritime SoN mission.

MatchedObjectDescriptor.QualificationSummary: Eligibility will be based upon a clear showing the applicant has education, training, and experience of the scope and quality sufficient to effectively carry-out the duties of the position. Candidates must exemplify the corporate perspective, leadership vision, broad experience and character needed in the SES corps not only to satisfy the immediate vacancy, but future vacancies which will occur in a variety of organizations, functions and locations. Candidates will not be hired based on their race, sex, color, religion, or national origin. In accordance with new OPM requirements to streamline Senior Executive Service (SES) hiring, applicants are no longer required to submit lengthy narrative essays, including those for Executive Core Qualifications (ECQs) or Mandatory Technical Qualifications (TQs), when applying. Instead, the initial application will be resume-only, capped at two pages. This change streamlines the application process and more closely aligns with private industry practices. Applicants identified for potential selection will have their ECQs assessed by undergoing a structured interview with the Office of Personnel Management (OPM) Qualifications Review Board (QRB). To meet the minimum qualification requirements for this position, you must show that you possess the education, Technical Qualifications (TQ), and Executive Core Qualifications (ECQ) related to this position within your resume (not to exceed 2 pages). Resumes over the 2-page limit will be disqualified. Your resume should include examples of experience, education, and accomplishments applicable to the qualification(s). If your resume does not reflect demonstrated evidence of the ECQs and TQs, you may not receive further consideration for the position. TECHNICAL QUALIFICATIONS (TQs): Your resume should demonstrate accomplishments that satisfy the technical qualifications. TQ1. Constitutional Literacy, Democratic Oversight, Civic Trust, Treaty/Statutory Compliance. Directs the development and legal review of all operational plans (OPLANs) to include nuclear employment concepts. Ensures that all plans conform strictly to Title 10 (Armed Forces) and Title 50 (War and National Defense) of the U.S. Code, international humanitarian law, and standing arms control treaties. Establishes and maintains transparent, authoritative channels of communication with congressional committees, the White House, and defense oversight bodies. Translates highly classified operational capabilities and requirements into clear, unclassified and classified briefings that support legislative oversight and safeguard the public trust. TQ2. Strategic Integration, Interagency Diplomacy, Portfolio Synchronization, Outcome Delivery. Acts as the primary "senior diplomat" for USSTRATCOM strategy, policy, and plans issues in Washington, D.C., representing the command's strategic equities with fierce diplomacy in high-stakes forums. Routinely briefs, advises, and negotiates policy and resource allocations with 4-Star General Officers, the Secretary and Undersecretaries of War/Defense, the Joint Staff Operations Deputies (OpsDeps), and White House National Security Council staff. Leverages collaborative executive authority to dismantle institutional barriers between Combatant Commands (CCMDs). Leads cross-functional, inter-organizational working groups to synchronize USSTRATCOM's global deterrence posture with the geographic and functional operations of partner commands, producing integrated, multi-domain options for the President. Deploys a mature, pre-existing network of high-level contacts across the Joint Staff, the Office of the Secretary of War (OSW)/Defense, the Department of Energy (DOE), the Department of State, and the Intelligence Community. Mobilizes this network to rapidly resolve coordination deadlocks and build consensus during fast-breaking strategic crises. Delivers highly integrated, timely, and credible strategic options to the President. Ensures these options combine kinetic and non-kinetic capabilities, are thoroughly vetted against adversary perceptions and force availability, and directly preserve presidential decision space during national security emergencies. Leading People: Demonstrated ability to lead and inspire a group toward meeting the organization's vision, mission, and goals, and to drive a high-performance, high-accountability culture. This includes, when necessary, the ability to lead people through change and to hold individuals accountable. ECQ 5. Achieving Results: Demonstrated ability to achieve both individual and organizational results, and to align results to stated goals from superiors. Please note: If you are a member of the SES or have been certified through successful participation in an OPM approved SES Candidate Development Program, or have SES reinstatement eligibility, you must attach proof (e.g., SF-50 or Certification by OPM's SES Qualifications Review Board) of your eligibility for noncompetitive appointment to the SES.

Details.JobSummary: As the Deputy Director for Plans and Policy (DJ5) at USSTRATCOM, you serve as the senior civilian executive leading global strategic deterrence during a complex shift to a multi-polar nuclear landscape. Working with the J5 Director, you oversee day-to-day operations and a diverse workforce. Your mission is dual-track: sustaining legacy systems while rapidly modernizing capabilities across cyber and space, acting as a key diplomat to OSW/OSD and the NSC.
Details.AgencyMarketingStatement: The mission of the United States Air Force is to fly, fight and win...airpower anytime, anywhere. To achieve that mission, the Air Force has a vision of Global Vigilance, Reach and Power. That vision orbits around three core competencies: Develop Airmen, Technology-to-Warfighting and Integrating Operations. Core competencies and distinctive capabilities are based on a shared commitment to three core values -- integrity first, service before self, and excellence in all we do.
MajorDuties: The Deputy Director for Plans and Policy (DJ5) at USSTRATCOM is the senior civilian executive responsible for ensuring that all strategic operational plans and nuclear employment concepts strictly align with Title 10 and Title 50 of the U.S. Code, international law, and arms control treaties. To maintain democratic oversight and safeguard public trust, the Deputy Director establishes transparent communication channels with congressional committees, the White House, and defense oversight bodies, translating highly classified capabilities into clear briefings. As the primary champion for human-in-the-loop systems integrity, the incumbent systematically audits artificial intelligence and machine learning integrations within warning systems to protect presidential decision-making authority. Operational efficiency is driven through calculated risk management, balancing the fail-safe sustainment of legacy platforms with the rapid scaling of modernized kinetic and non-kinetic capabilities. The Deputy Director exercises direct executive control over an operational budget of up to $9.2 million-including key portfolios like Deterrence Assurance Planning Support ($1.6M-$1.8M) and Tri-lab funding ($2.7M-$3.1M)-by streamlining contract integration and holding contractors to performance-based benchmarks. Efficiency is further enhanced by adopting advanced software, big data analytics, and cloud tools to automate routine administrative workflows, freeing human intelligence for high-priority strategic analysis. This role demands elite cognitive agility to transition between zero-defect nuclear operations and the agile thinking required to navigate space, cyber, and electromagnetic spectrum domains. Serving as the chief futurist, the Deputy Director leads long-range intelligence-fusion efforts to anticipate adversary technological breakthroughs, such as hypersonics and quantum communications, and preemptively adjusts USSTRATCOM's strategic posture. Applying authoritative technical expertise in Joint doctrine and nuclear command and control, the incumbent designs unified plans integrating conventional, nuclear, and non-kinetic options. Leading a highly specialized joint workforce of approximately 190 active military, 205 federal civilians, and 37 contractor personnel, the Deputy Director builds a collaborative culture of innovation and psychological safety where personnel can challenge outdated processes without reprisal. This leadership actively supports physical, mental, and professional resilience while cultivating future national security leaders through dedicated mentorship and succession planning for the Senior Executive Service and flag-officer ranks. To achieve critical results, the Deputy Director acts as USSTRATCOM's primary senior diplomat in Washington, D.C., negotiating policy and resource allocations with 4-star generals, the Secretary of War/Defense, the Joint Staff, and the National Security Council. The incumbent dismantles institutional silos between Combatant Commands by leading cross-functional working groups to synchronize global deterrence postures. By leveraging a mature, pre-existing network across the Joint Staff, OSW/OSD, the Department of Energy, the Department of State, and the Intelligence Community, the Deputy Director rapidly resolves coordination deadlocks during fast-breaking crises. Ultimately, these efforts deliver highly integrated, timely, and credible strategic options to the President, combining kinetic and non-kinetic capabilities to preserve vital presidential decision space during national security emergencies.

MatchedObjectDescriptor.QualificationSummary: Eligibility will be based upon a clear showing the applicant has training, education, and experience of the scope and quality sufficient to effectively carry-out the duties of the position. Candidates must exemplify the corporate perspective, leadership vision, broad experience and character needed in the SES corps not only to satisfy the immediate vacancy, but future vacancies which will occur in a variety of organizations, functions and locations. Candidates will not be hired based on their race, sex, color, religion, or national origin. In accordance with new OPM requirements to streamline Senior Executive Service (SES) hiring, applicants are no longer required to submit lengthy narrative essays, including those for Executive Core Qualifications (ECQs) or Mandatory Technical Qualifications (TQs), when applying. Instead, the initial application will be resume-only, capped at two pages. This change streamlines the application process and more closely aligns with private industry practices. Applicants identified for potential selection will have their ECQs assessed by undergoing a structured interview with the Office of Personnel Management (OPM) Qualifications Review Board (QRB). To meet the minimum qualification requirements for this position, you must show that you possess the Executive Core Qualifications (ECQ) and Technical Qualifications (TQ) related to this position within your resume (not to exceed 2 pages). Resumes over the 2-page limit will be disqualified. Your resume should include examples of experience, education, and accomplishments applicable to the qualification(s). If your resume does not reflect demonstrated evidence of the ECQs and TQs, you may not receive further consideration for the position. TECHNICAL QUALIFICATIONS (TQs): Your resume should demonstrate accomplishments that satisfy the technical qualifications. TQ1. Executive-level experience in program development and management; a high-level of personal initiative, creative problem solving skills, and the ability to rapidly formulate and communicate decisions; and the ability to present and defend independent positions at the highest levels of government. National recognition as evidenced by significant technical achievements and contributions; participation on national/international level committees and panels, etc.; high-level honors and awards; and other equivalent recognition are necessary. TQ2. A strong background in formulation of strategic and operational level military joint training, exercise, war gaming and assessment policies and plans related to USSTRATCOM mission areas. The position requires the incumbent to have strong knowledge of Department of War general business practices, joint exercise, training and war gaming programs, and possess the ability to develop or adapt policy as needed. Working knowledge of the National Security structure with emphasis on the Joint Staff, OSD, Services and unified and specific commands' role and communication lines is also necessary. EXECUTIVE CORE QUALIFICATIONS (ECQs): All new appointees to the Senior Executive Service (SES) under a career appointment will be assessed for executive competency against the five mandatory ECQs: ECQ 1. Commitment to the Rule of Law and the Principles of the American Founding: Demonstrated knowledge of the American system of government, commitment to uphold the Constitution and the rule of law, and commitment to serve the American people. ECQ 2. Driving Efficiency: Demonstrated ability to strategically and efficiently manage resources, budget effectively, cut wasteful spending, and pursue efficiency through process and technological upgrades. ECQ 3. Merit and Competence: Demonstrated knowledge, ability, and technical competence to effectively and reliably produce work that is of exceptional quality. ECQ 4. Leading People: Demonstrated ability to lead and inspire a group toward meeting the organization's vision, mission, and goals, and to drive a high-performance, high-accountability culture. This includes, when necessary, the ability to lead people through change and to hold individuals accountable. ECQ 5. Achieving Results: Demonstrated ability to achieve both individual and organizational results, and to align results to stated goals from superiors. Please note: If you are a member of the SES or have been certified through successful participation in an OPM approved SES Candidate Development Program, or have SES reinstatement eligibility, you must attach proof (e.g., SF-50 or Certification by OPM's SES Qualifications Review Board) of your eligibility for noncompetitive appointment to the SES.

Details.JobSummary: This leadership position is essential for providing global capabilities that support national, strategic, operational, and tactical requirements. The Director influences national policy, manages the Planning, Programming, Budgeting, and Execution (PPBE) process for training, and serves as a primary advocate for Command priorities. Additionally, the Director advises the Commander on highly complex issues and provides expert preparation for Congressional testimony.
Details.SubAgencyName: Joint Exercises, Training & Assessments Directorate, U.S. Strategic Command (USSTRATCOM)
Details.AgencyMarketingStatement: The mission of the United States Air Force is to fly, fight and win...airpower anytime, anywhere. To achieve that mission, the Air Force has a vision of Global Vigilance, Reach and Power. That vision orbits around three core competencies: Developing Airmen, Technology-to-Warfighting and Integrating Operations. Core competencies and distinctive capabilities are based on a shared commitment to three core values -- integrity first, service before self, and excellence in all we do.
MajorDuties: THIS VACANCY IS ONLY OPEN TO CURRENT DEPARTMENT OF WAR EXECUTIVES The Director of Joint Exercises, Training, and Assessments is a critical leadership position supporting the USSTRATCOM Commander and the Department of War (DoW). Acting as the primary representative to the Joint Staff, Office of the Secretary of War (OSW), other Combatant Commands, and Allied partners, the Director shapes national policy and ensures Command alignment with higher-echelon directives. They routinely coordinate with senior military and civilian leaders to advocate for USSTRATCOM requirements, provide expert counsel for Congressional testimony, and foster globally integrated operations. A central operational responsibility is the planning and execution of premier Tier 1 exercises, such as GLOBAL THUNDER and GLOBAL LIGHTNING, alongside vital Nuclear Command and Control (NC2) training programs. By managing the USSTRATCOM Wargame Center, the Director provides advanced analytical environments that refine cognitive problem-solving, reduce complexity, and enhance readiness across strategic deterrence, space, cyber, and missile defense missions. To inform leadership and shape future strategy, the Director leads comprehensive mission area assessments. This includes evaluating the Risk of Strategic Deterrence Failure (RoSDF) and measuring progress against the National Military Strategy and global campaign plans. These independent assessments generate critical insights for the J3, J5, and J8 directorates, directly influencing operational decisions, strategic investments, and 4-star input to the DoW. Beyond operational and assessment duties, the Director exercises full executive authority over personnel and resource management. They are responsible for recruiting, developing, and leading a diverse workforce while resolving complex issues across organizational lines. Furthermore, the Director provides rigorous fiscal oversight of the multi-million dollar Joint Training, Exercise, and Evaluation (JTEEP) budget, utilizing the PPBE process to ensure optimal resource allocation and mission effectiveness.

MatchedObjectDescriptor.QualificationSummary: Candidates should be committed to improving the efficiency of the Federal government, passionate about the ideals of our American republic, and committed to upholding the rule of law and the United States Constitution. Candidates will not be hired based on their race, sex, color, religion, or national origin. To meet the minimum qualification requirements for this position, you must show that you possess the Executive Core Qualifications (ECQ), and Technical Qualifications (TQ) related to this position within your resume - NOT TO EXCEED 2 PAGES. Resumes over the 2-page limit will be disqualified. Please see "Required Documents" section below for all resume formatting requirements. Your resume should include examples of experience, education, and accomplishments applicable to the qualification(s). If your resume does not reflect demonstrated evidence of these qualifications, you may not receive consideration for the position. Do NOT submit a separate narrative statement specifically addressing the Executive Core Qualifications (ECQs) or the Technical Qualifications (TQs). TECHNICAL QUALIFICATIONS (TQs): Your resume should demonstrate accomplishments that would satisfy the technical qualifications: TQ 1: Demonstrated senior executive experience leading complex technical organizations, translating strategic vision into measurable outcomes, and operating effectively across organizational boundaries under conditions of ambiguity and pressure. TQ 2: Comprehensive executive-level experience in program and portfolio management, encompassing systems engineering, DoW budgeting processes, modern digital infrastructure, and joint military operations to deliver complex technical capabilities. EXECUTIVE CORE QUALIFICATIONS (ECQs): In addition to the Technical Qualification Requirements listed above, all new entrants into the Senior Executive Service (SES) under a career appointment will be assessed for executive competency against the following five mandatory ECQs. If your 2-page resume does not reflect demonstrated evidence of the ECQs and TQs, you may not receive further consideration for the position. There are five ECQs: ECQ 1: Commitment to the Rule of Law and the Principles of the American Founding - This core qualification requires a demonstrated knowledge of the American system of government, commitment to uphold the Constitution and the rule of law, and commitment to serve the American people. Sub-Competencies: Knowledge of the American System of Government: Demonstrates understanding and appreciation of the American system of government, including the Constitution, the Bill of Rights, separation of powers, federalism, and the historical development of the American Nation. Commitment to the Rule of Law: Upholds the principles of the American Founding, including equality under the law and democratic self-government. Ensures the law is applied fairly and consistently. Civic-Mindedness: Stays up-to-date on important developments in American government and aligns organizational objectives and practices with presidential and public interests. Demonstrates a commitment to serve the American people. ECQ 2: Driving Efficiency - This core qualification involves the demonstrated ability to strategically and efficiently manage resources, budget effectively, cut wasteful spending, and pursue efficiency through process and technological upgrades. Sub-Competencies: Fiscal Responsibility: Strategically manages, allocates and monitors financial resources. Aligns priorities and initiatives to justify budget proposals. Monitors expenditures, cuts unnecessary costs, and uses cost-benefit analysis to set priorities. Managing Resources: Manages resources efficiently and effectively based on current and projected organizational goals, skills, budget considerations, and staffing needs. Leveraging Technology: Explores emerging technology and potential applications. Incorporates technology to enhance efficiency and achieve results. Ensures access to and security of technology systems. ECQ 3: Merit and Competence - This core qualification involves the demonstrated knowledge, ability and technical competence to effectively and reliably produce work that is of exceptional quality. Sub-Competencies: Technical Skill: Possesses the requisite technical knowledge and subject matter expertise to consistently produce timely, high-quality work. Is considered a strong contributor in his or her domain. Problem Solving: Engages in critical and data-driven thinking when diagnosing root causes and evaluating options. Identifies and promptly addresses the most pressing, high-priority problems. Agility and Resilience: Anticipates and adapts to change, new ideas, new information, and new conditions. Is committed to continuous improvement. Deals effectively with pressure and remains optimistic and persistent, even under adversity. ECQ 4: Leading People - This core qualification involves the demonstrated ability to lead and inspire a group toward meeting the organization's vision, mission, and goals, and to drive a high-performance, high-accountability culture. This includes, when necessary, the ability to lead people through change and to hold individuals accountable. Sub-Competencies: Accountability: Ensures that employees are appropriately recruited, selected, appraised, trained, and retained. Takes swift action to address performance- or conduct-based deficiencies in employees supervised. Holds self and others accountable for measurable high-quality, timely, and cost-effective results. Developing Others: Recognizes and rewards outstanding achievement in others. Develops the ability of others to perform and contribute to the organization by providing opportunities to learn through formal and informal methods. Cultivates a dynamic environment in which employees are not afraid to make mistakes. Executive Judgement: Makes well-reasoned, timely, and effective decisions and considers short- and long-term implications. Communicates effectively with stakeholders across all organizational levels, sharing and guarding information where appropriate. ECQ 5: Achieving Results - This core qualification involves the demonstrated ability to achieve both individual and organizational results, and to align results to stated goals from superiors. Sub-Competencies: Operational Mindset: Effectively translates strategies into actionable steps and processes. Partners effectively with stakeholders to drive adoption and addresses blockers to ensure successful implementation. Innovation: Applies creativity to improving products and processes, challenges convention, takes measured risks, and considers ways to simplify and remove unnecessary requirements. Strategic Thinking: Formulates objectives and priorities and implements plans consistent with the long-term interests of the organization by evaluating conditions, resources, capabilities, constraints, and organizational goals and values. Note: If you are a member of the SES or have been certified through successful participation in an OPM approved SES Candidate Development Program (SESCDP), or have SES reinstatement eligibility, you must attach proof (e.g., SF-50, Certification by OPM's SES Qualifications Review Board (QRB)) of your eligibility for noncompetitive appointment to the SES. See "Required Documents" section for additional information.

Details.JobSummary: The Principal Director, Mission Engineering and Integration Activity (MEIA), is the senior career executive and principal advisor to the Deputy Assistant Secretary of War for Mission Integration. The incumbent provides continuity, executive management, technical integration, and disciplined execution for MEIA as a Department-wide mission engineering reform effort.
Details.SubAgencyName: Office of the Under Secretary of War for Research and Engineering
Details.AgencyMarketingStatement: This position is in the Senior Executive Service (SES), a small, elite group of top government leaders. SES members possess a diverse portfolio of experiences including strong skills to lead across organizations. As a Senior Executive, you will influence the direction of innovation and transformation of the federal government and lead the next generation of public servants. The Office of the Secretary of War (OSW) is the principal staff element of the Secretary of War in the exercise of policy development, planning, resource management, and program evaluation responsibilities. OSW includes the Offices of the Secretary and Deputy Secretary of War, Under Secretaries of War, Assistant Secretaries of War, General Counsel of the DoW; Director of Cost Assessment and Program Evaluation; Inspector General of the DoW; Director of Operational Test and Evaluation; Chief Information Officer of the DoW; Assistant to the Secretary of War for Public Affairs; Chief Digital and Artificial Intelligence Officer; and the Director of Administration and Management.
MajorDuties: The Principal Director, Mission Engineering and Integration Activity (MEIA), leads a large, multidisciplinary enterprise of military, civilian, Federally Funded Research and Development Centers, University Affiliated Research Center, and contractor personnel, and performs the following major functions: Major duties and responsibilities include, but are not limited to: Directs the day-to-day operations, administration, and execution of the MEIA enterprise and serves as the principal source of organizational continuity across changes in political leadership, priorities, personnel, and fiscal conditions. Provides executive integration and oversight across the full range of MEIA functions to ensure they operate as one Department-level enterprise rather than as independent activities. Directs advanced mission engineering and systems-of-systems analysis to decompose Blue and adversary kill chains, identify limiting factors and capability gaps, and develop integrated options that create measurable operational advantage. Provides executive oversight of MEIA programs, projects, contracts, analytic efforts, digital products, infrastructure, and capability-development initiatives; maintains accountability for cost, schedule, performance, technical risk, transition, and return on investment. Leads MEIA participation in the Department Planning, Programming, Budgeting, and Execution process and translates mission engineering findings into executable resource options, Program Element impacts, budget recommendations, budget priorities, spend plans, and transition strategies. Institutionalizes business case analysis and return on investment as core MEIA decision disciplines for capability development and Department resource decisions. Provides executive oversight of MEIA multi-cloud, multi-classification digital environments supporting analysis, mission engineering, modeling and simulation, Artificial Intelligence, data integration, software development, and secure collaboration. Provides executive oversight of structured industry engagement and technical due diligence to identify and assess commercial and defense technologies relevant to priority mission problems. Demonstrated senior executive experience leading complex technical organizations, translating strategic vision into measurable outcomes, and operating effectively across organizational boundaries under conditions of ambiguity and pressure.

MatchedObjectDescriptor.QualificationSummary: Candidates should be committed to improving the efficiency of the Federal government, passionate about the ideals of our American republic, and committed to upholding the rule of law and the United States Constitution. Candidates will not be hired based on their race, sex, color, religion, or national origin. To meet the minimum qualification requirements for this position, you must show that you possess the Executive Core Qualifications (ECQ), and Technical Qualifications (TQ) related to this position within your resume - NOT TO EXCEED 2 PAGES. Resumes over the 2-page limit will be disqualified. Please see "Required Documents" section below for all resume formatting requirements. Your resume should include examples of experience, education, and accomplishments applicable to the qualification(s). If your resume does not reflect demonstrated evidence of these qualifications, you may not receive consideration for the position. Do NOT submit a separate narrative statement specifically addressing the Executive Core Qualifications (ECQs) or the Technical Qualifications (TQs). TECHNICAL QUALIFICATIONS (TQs): Your resume should demonstrate accomplishments that would satisfy the technical qualifications: TQ 1: Proven executive and managerial abilities, including in-depth knowledge and experience in analysis, planning, programming and budgeting and Defense systems procedures, as well as knowledge of the operation, mission and management concepts and procedures of DoW components to include the Reserve Component. TQ 2: The ability to synthesize and analyze broad, complex policy, strategy, program or procedural issues utilizing identified metrics with a view toward quantifying the implication in relation to functional areas and DoW readiness in general. EXECUTIVE CORE QUALIFICATIONS (ECQs): In addition to the Technical Qualification Requirements listed above, all new entrants into the Senior Executive Service (SES) under a career appointment will be assessed for executive competency against the following five mandatory ECQs. If your 2-page resume does not reflect demonstrated evidence of the ECQs and TQs, you may not receive further consideration for the position. There are five ECQs: ECQ 1: Commitment to the Rule of Law and the Principles of the American Founding - This core qualification requires a demonstrated knowledge of the American system of government, commitment to uphold the Constitution and the rule of law, and commitment to serve the American people. Sub-Competencies: Knowledge of the American System of Government: Demonstrates understanding and appreciation of the American system of government, including the Constitution, the Bill of Rights, separation of powers, federalism, and the historical development of the American Nation. Commitment to the Rule of Law: Upholds the principles of the American Founding, including equality under the law and democratic self-government. Ensures the law is applied fairly and consistently. Civic-Mindedness: Stays up-to-date on important developments in American government and aligns organizational objectives and practices with presidential and public interests. Demonstrates a commitment to serve the American people. ECQ 2: Driving Efficiency - This core qualification involves the demonstrated ability to strategically and efficiently manage resources, budget effectively, cut wasteful spending, and pursue efficiency through process and technological upgrades. Sub-Competencies: Fiscal Responsibility: Strategically manages, allocates and monitors financial resources. Aligns priorities and initiatives to justify budget proposals. Monitors expenditures, cuts unnecessary costs, and uses cost-benefit analysis to set priorities. Managing Resources: Manages resources efficiently and effectively based on current and projected organizational goals, skills, budget considerations, and staffing needs. Leveraging Technology: Explores emerging technology and potential applications. Incorporates technology to enhance efficiency and achieve results. Ensures access to and security of technology systems. ECQ 3: Merit and Competence - This core qualification involves the demonstrated knowledge, ability and technical competence to effectively and reliably produce work that is of exceptional quality. Sub-Competencies: Technical Skill: Possesses the requisite technical knowledge and subject matter expertise to consistently produce timely, high-quality work. Is considered a strong contributor in his or her domain. Problem Solving: Engages in critical and data-driven thinking when diagnosing root causes and evaluating options. Identifies and promptly addresses the most pressing, high-priority problems. Agility and Resilience: Anticipates and adapts to change, new ideas, new information, and new conditions. Is committed to continuous improvement. Deals effectively with pressure and remains optimistic and persistent, even under adversity. ECQ 4: Leading People - This core qualification involves the demonstrated ability to lead and inspire a group toward meeting the organization's vision, mission, and goals, and to drive a high-performance, high-accountability culture. This includes, when necessary, the ability to lead people through change and to hold individuals accountable. Sub-Competencies: Accountability: Ensures that employees are appropriately recruited, selected, appraised, trained, and retained. Takes swift action to address performance- or conduct-based deficiencies in employees supervised. Holds self and others accountable for measurable high-quality, timely, and cost-effective results. Developing Others: Recognizes and rewards outstanding achievement in others. Develops the ability of others to perform and contribute to the organization by providing opportunities to learn through formal and informal methods. Cultivates a dynamic environment in which employees are not afraid to make mistakes. Executive Judgement: Makes well-reasoned, timely, and effective decisions and considers short- and long-term implications. Communicates effectively with stakeholders across all organizational levels, sharing and guarding information where appropriate. ECQ 5: Achieving Results - This core qualification involves the demonstrated ability to achieve both individual and organizational results, and to align results to stated goals from superiors. Sub-Competencies: Operational Mindset: Effectively translates strategies into actionable steps and processes. Partners effectively with stakeholders to drive adoption and addresses blockers to ensure successful implementation. Innovation: Applies creativity to improving products and processes, challenges convention, takes measured risks, and considers ways to simplify and remove unnecessary requirements. Strategic Thinking: Formulates objectives and priorities and implements plans consistent with the long-term interests of the organization by evaluating conditions, resources, capabilities, constraints, and organizational goals and values. See "Required Documents" section for additional information.

Details.JobSummary: The Principal Deputy Assistant Secretary of War for Readiness (PDASW(R)) serves as the principal advisor to the Assistant Secretary of War for Readiness, providing executive leadership, integration, and oversight of Department-wide readiness, policies, programs, plans, budgets, assessments and strategic initiatives. The PDASW(R) leads the three enterprise readiness portfolios, Strategic Readiness, Warfighter Development, and Occupational Readiness and Safety.

Details.AgencyMarketingStatement: This position is in the Senior Executive Service (SES), a small, elite group of top government leaders. SES members possess a diverse portfolio of experiences including strong skills to lead across organizations. As a Senior Executive, you will influence the direction of innovation and transformation of the federal government and lead the next generation of public servants. The Office of the Secretary of War (OSW) is the principal staff element of the Secretary of War in the exercise of policy development, planning, resource management, and program evaluation responsibilities. OSW includes the Offices of the Secretary and Deputy Secretary of War, Under Secretaries of War, Assistant Secretaries of War, General Counsel of the DoW; Director of Cost Assessment and Program Evaluation; Inspector General of the DoW; Director of Operational Test and Evaluation; Chief Information Officer of the DoW; Assistant to the Secretary of War for Public Affairs; Chief Digital and Artificial Intelligence Officer; and the Director of Administration and Management.
MajorDuties: Major duties and responsibilities include, but are not limited to: Strategic Readiness. Serves as the focal point within the Department of War (DoW) for all DoW policies, plans, and guidance related to the readiness of the Total Force (Active and Reserve Components, DoW Civilians, and Contractors supporting DoW) and the readiness of the Combatant Commands to execute specified plans. Included in this duty is analysis of the readiness implications of major strategy and force alternatives, coordination of the process for establishing readiness standards, and research into the fundamental relationship between the readiness of the forces and their ability to execute the National Defense Strategy; serves as the Department lead for all readiness strategic communication. Warfighter Development. Develops and promulgates policies, plans, programs, budgets, and other activities necessary to develop, guide, measure, implement, assess, and oversee all aspects of military education. This includes: professional development, the Department's strategic policy planning for English and foreign language, culture, and regional expertise, and the policies and programs for the National Security Education Program; develops policy; and provides transition assistance and credentialing policy and program oversight to promote, advance and instill a culture of career ready Service members. Occupation Readiness and Safety. Initiates, develops, and oversees DoW policies and programs, and coordinates DoW positions across: the Department; federal, state and local government; the private sector; and academia. Represents the Department in national and international forums sponsored by government and industry. Prepares expert testimony on budgetary and technical matters to be provided to congressional committees and staff. Fields, develops, and coordinates legislative initiatives addressing readiness of the Total Force, to include reserve component policy and statute, ensuring DoW positions are appropriately enacted or refined.

Our Vision DCSA's elite security experts illuminate national security risks to empower faster, smarter decision-making that protects American innovation and resilience to enable mission success. DCSA Strategic Execution Plan The Defense Counterintelligence and Security Agency stands at the intersection of government-wide trusted workforce, national security, and industrial base protection. Guided by the Secretary of War's National Defense Strategy, Deputy Secretary's Warfighting Acquisition Transformation efforts, and Trusted Workforce 2.0, our mission is to deliver data-driven, threat-informed, and customer-trusted security services at scale.
